newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Australia mine cos good picks-fund mgr.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Australia mine cos good picks-fund mgr.

text.p: Australian mining stocks offer good chaices for investors seeking exposure in Australia, one of the top executives of Sydney's EquitiLink Ltd said.

Lawrence Freedman, director of EquitiLink's First Australia Fund Inc and First Australia Prime Income Fund Inc, told Reuters that Australia and its mine companies were poised to take advantage of robust economic growth in Asia, especially China.
Freedman said the companies' history of working in less-developed countries would give it an edge over most U.S. mining companies seeking to enter the same areas.
"Wherever the ore is in a Third World country, you've got First World technology from Australian companies" to exploit it, said Freedman, who was in New York to meet potential investors.
"They've been very successful at it and U.S. companies, or most of them, have not been."
He said another advantage for mining companies was that Australia and its mineral resources had a ready market for their materials in the booming economies in Asia.
The companies also would be helped as low world stockpiles of lead, zinc, tin, copper and aluminum need to be replaced.
Among Freedman's favored stocks were such large capitalization companies as Pasminco Ltd and Woodside Petroleum Ltd and mid-sized companies, such as Great Central Mines NL.
Among small companies, his picks included Amalg Resources NL, a producer of base metals and gold.
He said the large companies had "reasonable value" and the small-cap stocks were generally undervalued.
